::: {.center-align .hand-blue} [beanumber.github.io/quarto-life-hacks-jsm26](https://beanumber.github.io/quarto-life-hacks-jsm26/) :::
::: incremental - **Colin** :: automate all the things - **Grayson** :: diagnostic plots with grammar of graphics - **Adam** :: stop repeating yourself -- shared R resources - **William** :: one source, three documents -- the LTS format ::: ## `grep -i "why we do this"` {.prompt}
Grayson :: **diagnostic plots with gg**
::: {.hack} > I believe that learning to code while learning statistics helps students gain a deeper understanding of the material. ::: ::: {.hack .fragment} > But nowadays, fewer people agree with me! ::: ## `plot a regression line` {.prompt} ::: {.chat} Create a scatterplot of miles per gallon (mpg) vs. displacement (disp) in mtcars, and overlay the regression line for predicting mpg from disp. ::: . . . ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot( mtcars, aes(x = disp, y = mpg) ) + geom_point() + geom_smooth( method = "lm", se = FALSE ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](discussion_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: With Claude Opus 4.8 (via Posit AI). ## `plot a regression line` {.prompt} ::: {.chat} Now limit to cars with displacement below 200. ::: . . . ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} mtcars |> filter(disp < 200) |> ggplot(aes(x = disp, y = mpg)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth( method = "lm", se = FALSE ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](discussion_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: With Claude Opus 4.8 (via Posit AI). ## `plot which regression line?` {.prompt} ::: {.cell layout-ncol="2"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](discussion_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](discussion_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-2.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column .fragment} ```r ... + coord_cartesian( xlim = c(60, 200) ) ``` ::: ::: {.column .fragment} ```r ... + xlim(60, 200) ``` ::: ::: ## `plot which regression line?` {.prompt} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](discussion_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=576} ::: ::: ## `R ggplot(mod)` {.prompt}
Grayson :: **diagnostic plots with gg**
![](images/gglm.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="gglm code and a Residuals vs Fitted plot colored by sex" width="600"} ## `autoAlt --describe` {.prompt}
Adam :: **alt text, automatically**
::: {.hack} > Use LLM to generate the alt text for my slides, notes, etc. ::: . . . ::: {.similar} Reminds me of... [numbats.github.io/autoAlt](https://numbats.github.io/autoAlt/index.html)
[Maliny Po](https://github.com/maliny12) autoAlt is an R package for automatically generating alt-text from qmd and rmd files. The `generate_alt_text()` function uses **ellmer** and **BrailleR** to create alt-text for plots in documents. ::: ## `curl assessment --hack` {.prompt}
Adam :: **stop repeating yourself**
::: hack > Devise additional quiz questions for standards-based grading using LLMs ::: . . . ::: {.my-experience .incremental} My experience... - Generate *a lot* more than you need - Pick a few good starting points and improve them - The hack: let AI give you raw material to sculpt ::: ## `simulate --from-table` {.prompt}
Adam :: **stop repeating yourself**
::: hack > Simulating data to match examples in journal articles when all you have is a table or a plot. ::: ::: {.my-experience .larger} [{{< fa heart >}}]{.fragment} [/ {{< fa face-grimace >}}]{.fragment} ::: ## `make packages` {.prompt}
Colin + William
::: {.hack} Productivity as an R package / the grind of course-ops, packaged - Colin -- `ghclass`, `q2r`, `markermd` - William -- `moodleR` ::: ::: {.my-experience .incremental} The pattern: **wrap the annoying part, ship it, reuse it** ::: ## `moodlequiz --deploy` {.prompt}
William :: **moodlequiz**
::: hack **moodleR** Interact with a Moodle Course Page via Headless Chrome ::: ::: {.similar .fragment} Reminds me of... [numbats.github.io/moodlequiz](https://numbats.github.io/moodlequiz/)
[Mitchell O'Hara-Wild](https://github.com/mitchelloharawild) **moodlequiz** package allows the creation of Moodle quiz questions using literate programming with R Markdown. ::: ## `cat themes.log` {.prompt} ::: incremental - **One source of truth** -- write it once, render it everywhere (LTS, moodlequiz) - **Wrap the drudgery** -- if you do it twice, make it a package (ghclass, q2r, markermd) - **AI as an intern, not an author** -- draft quizzes, sim data, alt text; *you* keep judgment - **Coding *is* the pedagogy** -- not a distraction from stats, but a deeper way in ::: ## `life hacking for educators` {.prompt background-color="#04060d"} ::: {.center-align .large .neon-green .cursor} questions? :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
